newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS-Milan stocks take wing, Italy back in favour.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Milan stocks take wing, Italy back in favour.

text.p: Milan stocks are taking wing, after months of doing little while other share markets boomed, and analysts say international investors are finally taking notice of Italy.
The blue-chip Mib30 index, which had hit a historic peak at 20,140 by mid-afternoon on Friday, has smashed record after record in the last few days.
It has been driven to new heights by derivatives trades and optimism over Italy's chances of joining Europe's single currency at its proposed January 1999 start.

"Italy's been ignored for such a long time and it's been flat in relation to other markets in Europe and the United States. So it now looks like a good opportunity to buy cheaply," said Anthony Mannara, who is responsible for institutional sales at brokers Milla Sim.

Volume on Friday hit a huge 3.53 trillion lire ($2.1 billion) just at the market opening as investors scrambled to cover options and futures positions expiring at the start of trade. This is the largest turnover ever for an entire day's trading, the bourse council said.
By 1240 GMT the blue-chip Mib30 index was 1.57 percent up at 20,140 and the all-share Mibtel 1.32 percent higher at 13,237.
The key question now is whether the stock market can sustain such a rally after months of drifting.
"It's important to see today and the next two trading days what direction the market wants to take," said Marco Nascimbeni, equity specialist at Merrill Lynch Capital Markets Bank.
He added that if the index sustained its rise above 20,000, it could move up in the direction of 22,000.
Analysts say there has been more activity from foreign investors.

Domestic investors have experienced liquidity problems recently as they made room in their portfolios for a third tranche of shares in state controlled energy giant ENI, which will be up for public offer next week.
"There's been a change in attitude to Italy as people see it having more chance of getting into the first round of European monetary union," Nascimbeni said.

The head of share dealing at one Italian bank, who asked not to be named, said he believed the market had further to go, helped by progress on key parliamentary reforms and by Italy's continuing low inflation and the prospect for an eventual cut in official interest rates.
"Even if we're not expecting another rate cut soon, what really matters is that one is still expected sometime," he said.

For now, he added, "inflation is stable to improving and political issues are not creating any trouble short term" but talks between the government, trade unions and employees on reforming welfare state spending, particularly pensions, might hinder progress later.
He was cautious, not ruling out a slip back after the sharp gains of the last few days made the market overbought.
The area around 19,000 would provide a possible prop in the event of a retracement and he wondered if the political issues and economic fundamentals were strong enough to let the market gain much.
Analysts said, however, that sectors with potential were insurance, with rumours of change at insurer Fondiaria, and small capitalised stocks, since most action so far had touched blue-chips.
Mannara said interest was growing in the banking sector where investors were finally seeing changes to the industry to make it become more efficient.
But overall investors were having to revalue individual target prices' given the market's gains. "What you're seeing is a new perspective being put on prices," Mannara said. ($1=1,691 lire)
